title: 10th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with prayers, attendance and the agenda. Most of the part was a question session with the Minister of Islamic Affairs, Dr. Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed, covering delayed mosque and Islamic centre projects in several islands, the Hajj Corporation (its hotel plans, board, quotas and a promised law), halal tourism and mosque design; the Chair repeatedly called members to order and ordered the Kendhoo member to leave the chamber. After a recess (10:28 to 11:01) the Chair referred the Media and Broadcasting Commission chair matter to a committee and the North Galolhu member's resolution on health cover for foreign spouses of Maldivians went to preliminary debate, which was still under way when this part ends. Some attendance figures in the text are garbled, so the official travel count is left blank. Members finished debating a non-binding resolution asking parliament's view on foreign spouses of Maldivians who do not get Aasandha health coverage. Speakers mostly backed the idea of basic health care but argued over cost, residency rules and past governments' records. After a break the resolution was accepted for consideration 47-0 and sent to the Social Committee. A government bill amending the Special Economic Zones Act (24/2014) was also accepted for consideration, 41-6, and sent to a committee of the whole Majlis. Some words at the start of the part are cut off and the text is partly garbled, so the opening speaker is not named.

items.outcome: minister answered; follow-up questions from many members

items.title: Resolution introduced by the Kendhoo member on delayed flat handovers and the Hulhumale' Phase 3 and Gedhoruveriya housing schemes

items.outcome: both passed the vote to be accepted for consideration

speakers.name: Dr. Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed
positions: As Minister of Islamic Affairs, said the Kendhoo mosque contract is being terminated through legal steps and no opening date can be given.
Said the Hajj Corporation board decides its internal matters, the ministry only advises, and a law placing it under ministry oversight is being drafted.
Said mosque design and cost are being reviewed and that Islamic centres are meant to serve educational and social needs, not only prayer.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked whether any company is unpaid for mosque or Islamic centre projects, and when the Thoddoo mosque promised by the President will start.
Asked about money collected by a group for Umrah trips and whether a halal tourism plan exists.
Asked about plans to handle religious issues during the tourism high season on local tourism islands.
Noted foreign spouses are already on an insurance scheme and suggested moving them to Aasandha for a fee, with the committee to study details.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked whether the Hajj Corporation's move into the tourist hotel business was known to the Minister and what work was done.
Said mosque designs and sound systems need input, since some mosques are too loud inside.
Presented his resolution to learn members' views on foreign spouses of Maldivians lacking Aasandha health cover.
As the mover, said 552 foreign spouses were recorded in 2024, described the issue as one of rights, and asked members to vote it to committee.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked when the Quran centre will start work in Kela.
Asked when a tsunami-damaged mosque in Filladhoo will be rebuilt.
In the debate, backed the resolution on foreign spouses and said long-resident spouses need a proper, planned arrangement.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked how much of the Kendhoo mosque is built after MVR 2.8 million was paid to the contractor under the previous government.
Asked about the progress of a large mosque project.
Raised a microphone problem and referred to events earlier in the sitting; his speech is cut off at the end of this part.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked when the mosque being built in Dhondigama, Fuvahmulah, will finish.
Asked how Friday sermon topics are chosen and whether waqf buildings give the income they should.
Said many foreign spouses lack Aasandha cover but urged careful thought about cost and about securing citizens' own health coverage first.

speakers.name: Maaroof Zakir
positions: Asked why the Kendhoo mosque project is late, when it will open, and what progress and funds are involved.
Was named by the Chair and told to leave the chamber after repeated calls to sit down and follow the Rules.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked whether the Maradhoo mosque promised for March can be opened soon.
Asked whether the Hajj Corporation board format was discussed with the President or cabinet before it was set.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked why Quran reading courses were halted at the centre and why the second semester of the Level 4 course started late.
Asked whether visible bikinis at resorts mean it is not halal tourism, and how the Hajj Corporation recruits its helpers.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Asked what the ruling is on betraying funds given to build mosques and whether Muslims should trust such people.
Responded to earlier remarks about 2012, saying inquiry committees had not treated it as a coup.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked whether any company is unpaid for mosque or Islamic centre projects and when Thinadhoo's project will start.
Asked how much authority the Minister has over the Hajj Corporation and whether work can be given to suitable parties.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Asked when practical work on the Ihavandhoo Islamic centre will start.
In the debate, said he wants to help foreign spouses but the state's debt and health costs limit what it can afford.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said the chamber's conduct that morning was poor and asked the Chair to ensure it does not repeat.
In the debate, said foreign spouses who have lived here for many years deserve fairer treatment and a study of the rules.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked when work will begin on the mosque in Feevak that the President announced.
Said foreign spouses' health access could be handled through residency-based rules under existing law, and that past governments had not fixed it.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Asked when practical work will start on the Islamic centre planned in R. Meedhoo.
In the debate, backed easier Aasandha access for foreign spouses under clear rules, citing health costs and Singapore's tiered visas.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Asked when the finished Islamic centre in Dhidhdhoo will open and how much the government spent on it.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked how far work to clear the Thulhaadhoo mosque is, when it will open, and which company was given the work.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked when work on an Islamic centre in Kulhudhuffushi will start, how waqf funding will work, and the state of the Islamic Civilisation plan.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked about the Hithadhoo Islamic centre, said the contractor reports unpaid bills, and asked if it will finish within two or three years.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked how halal tourism is defined and whether the azan can be made louder in Hulhumale' Phase 1.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Asked the Minister about reports that Hajj quota was shared out through the President's Office under the previous government.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked about media reports that people with major illnesses would be barred from Hajj and whether that was a government decision.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked what the ministry's role is in sending people on Hajj and who writes the Friday sermons.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Asked whether the ministry is doing any work to increase the Hajj quota.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Asked for a faster solution for the overcrowded Zikra mosque on Majeedhee Magu, where worshippers pray outside.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Asked what thinking guides mosque design, saying some designs look like factories rather than Islamic buildings.

speakers.name: Asadhulla Shihab
positions: Asked when work on the stalled mosque in Gemanafushi will restart.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked whether the ministry plans an Islamic centre in Velidhoo, the largest island in Noonu Atoll.

speakers.name: Hussain Imran Latheef
positions: Asked about the Hajj backlog built up during COVID and how elderly people in the queue can be helped.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Said basic human services should reach everyone, and wanted the issue weighed alongside welfare problems of Maldivians themselves, such as single parents and housing.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Backed the intent but wanted the finances and eligibility rules studied, such as a minimum length of residence, before any change to the law.

decisions: The Chair announced 30 November 2025 as the committee deadline for the resolution on the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010).
The Chair named the Kendhoo member, Maaroof Zakir, and ordered him to leave the chamber after repeated warnings.
The matter of appointing the chair of the Media and Broadcasting Commission was referred to the Independent Institutions Committee.
The first reading of the Kendhoo member's resolution on delayed flat handovers was announced.
Preliminary debate began on the North Galolhu member's resolution on Aasandha cover for foreign spouses; it had not concluded by the end of this part.
Resolution on Aasandha cover for foreign spouses accepted for consideration and sent to the Social Committee under rule 106(r).
Special Economic Zones Act amendment bill accepted for consideration and sent to a committee of the whole Majlis under rule 106(r).
The chair sent a damaged-microphone dispute between two members (Inguraidhoo and South Hulhumale' desks) to the Conduct Committee.
The chair noted that ministers did not attend question time and said they have been rescheduled to appear.
Next sitting set for Monday 27 October 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept the Aasandha-for-foreign-spouses resolution for consideration
Accept the Special Economic Zones Act (24/2014) amendment bill for consideration
